subject.name: Chemistry
subject.examPattern: Extended: Paper 2 MCQ 45 min, 40 questions + Paper 4 Theory 1 h 15, 80 marks (~6–8 structured questions) + Paper 6 ATP 1 h, 40 marks (or P5 Practical). Weights 30/50/20. Grades A*–G.

subtopics.name: Solubility rules for salts, hydroxides and carbonates
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: General solubility rules of sodium, potassium, ammonium and nitrate salts; reactions of acids (IGCSE ch 11)

subtopics.name: Preparing a soluble salt from an acid and an excess insoluble base or carbonate
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Neutralisation and reactions of acids with bases and carbonates (IGCSE ch 11); filtration and crystallisation

subtopics.name: Preparing a soluble salt by titration of an acid with an alkali
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Titration calculations (IGCSE ch 5); indicators and end points

subtopics.name: Preparing an insoluble salt by precipitation
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Solubility rules for salts; writing ionic equations (IGCSE ch 4)

subtopics.name: Hydrated and anhydrous salts and water of crystallisation
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Percentage composition and empirical formula calculations (IGCSE ch 5); hydrated/anhydrous copper(II) sulfate

subtopics.name: Arrangement of elements in groups and periods; change from metallic to non-metallic character across a period
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Electronic configuration and group/period number (IGCSE ch 2)

subtopics.name: Group I alkali metals: physical properties, reactions with water and predicting trends
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Electronic configuration; Arrangement of the Periodic Table; metal + water word equations

subtopics.name: Group VII halogens: colours, physical states, trends and displacement reactions
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Arrangement of the Periodic Table; oxidation and reduction as electron transfer (IGCSE ch 10)

subtopics.name: Transition elements: high density, variable oxidation numbers, coloured compounds and catalysts
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Oxidation numbers and Roman numerals (IGCSE ch 10); properties of metals

subtopics.name: Noble gases: unreactivity explained by electronic configuration and uses
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Full outer shells in electronic configuration (IGCSE ch 2)

subtopics.name: Physical and chemical properties of metals: reactions with dilute acids, water and oxygen
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Metallic bonding (IGCSE ch 3); reactions of acids with metals (IGCSE ch 11)

subtopics.name: Alloys as mixtures; explaining why alloys are harder and stronger than pure metals
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Metallic bonding and layers of positive ions sliding (IGCSE ch 3)

subtopics.name: Uses of metals and alloys related to their properties: aluminium, copper, brass and stainless steel
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Physical properties of metals and alloys

subtopics.name: The reactivity series: reactions of metals with cold water, steam and dilute hydrochloric acid
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Physical and chemical properties of metals; tests for hydrogen gas

subtopics.name: Displacement reactions of metals with aqueous ions and metal oxides
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: The reactivity series; oxidation and reduction as electron transfer and ionic equations (IGCSE ch 4, 10)

subtopics.name: Explaining reactivity as the tendency of a metal to form positive ions; apparent unreactivity of aluminium
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Electronic configuration and ion formation (IGCSE ch 2-3); The reactivity series

subtopics.name: Relating the method of extraction to the reactivity series; reduction with carbon
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: The reactivity series; reduction as loss of oxygen (IGCSE ch 10)

subtopics.name: Extraction of iron from hematite in the blast furnace, including symbol equations
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Reduction with carbon; balancing symbol equations (IGCSE ch 4)

subtopics.name: Extraction of aluminium from purified bauxite by electrolysis with cryolite
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Electrolysis of molten compounds and half-equations (IGCSE ch 6)

subtopics.name: Rusting of iron and steel; barrier methods, galvanising and sacrificial protection
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Displacement reactions and reactivity series; oxidation as electron loss

subtopics.name: Water: chemical tests for water, treatment of the domestic water supply and pollutants in water
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Tests with anhydrous copper(II) sulfate and cobalt(II) chloride; filtration (Lower Secondary science)

subtopics.name: Fertilisers: NPK, ammonium salts and nitrates for plant growth
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Haber process (IGCSE ch 9); Preparing a soluble salt

subtopics.name: Composition of clean, dry air and sources and effects of air pollutants (CO, NOx, SO2, particulates)
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Elements, compounds and mixtures (IGCSE ch 2); combustion of fuels

subtopics.name: Greenhouse gases, climate change and reducing pollution; catalytic converters and photosynthesis
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Composition of air and pollutants; exothermic combustion (IGCSE ch 7); redox in catalytic converters

subtopics.name: Organic formulae: molecular, general, structural and displayed formulae
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Covalent bonding in simple molecules (IGCSE ch 3); valency of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen

subtopics.name: Naming organic compounds from functional groups and chain length (up to four carbons)
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Organic formulae; counting carbon atoms

subtopics.name: Homologous series and their general characteristics
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Organic formulae; Naming organic compounds

subtopics.name: Structural isomers: same molecular formula, different structural formula
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Organic formulae: displayed and structural

subtopics.name: Alkanes: complete combustion and substitution reaction with chlorine in UV light
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Homologous series; balancing combustion equations (IGCSE ch 4)

subtopics.name: Cracking of alkanes and addition reactions of alkenes; distinguishing with aqueous bromine
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Alkanes and saturated vs unsaturated bonds; Structural isomers

subtopics.name: Ethanol: manufacture by fermentation and by catalytic addition of steam to ethene; combustion and uses
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Addition reactions of alkenes; conditions for equilibrium (IGCSE ch 9)

subtopics.name: Carboxylic acids: reactions as weak acids and esterification with alcohols
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Ethanol reactions; strong and weak acids (IGCSE ch 11)

subtopics.name: Petroleum and natural gas as fuels; fractional distillation of petroleum and uses of fractions
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Boiling points and changes of state (IGCSE ch 1); Alkanes as fuels

subtopics.name: Addition polymerisation: poly(ethene) and deducing monomers and repeat units
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Addition reactions of alkenes; displayed formulae

subtopics.name: Condensation polymers: nylon (polyamide), PET (polyester) and proteins from amino acids
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Addition polymerisation; esterification of carboxylic acids

subtopics.name: Plastics: properties, disposal problems and recycling of PET
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Addition polymerisation; environmental pollution (Chemistry of Our Environment)

subtopics.name: Choosing apparatus to measure time, temperature, mass and volume; accuracy of measurements
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Reading scales and units (Lower Secondary science); significant figures

subtopics.name: Solvents, solutes, solutions and saturated solutions; choosing a separation method
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Elements, compounds and mixtures (IGCSE ch 2); solubility

subtopics.name: Filtration, crystallisation, simple distillation and fractional distillation
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Choosing a separation method; boiling points and changes of state (IGCSE ch 1)

subtopics.name: Paper chromatography, locating agents and Rf values; assessing purity from melting and boiling points
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Choosing a separation method; dividing distances to give a ratio

subtopics.name: Identifying aqueous cations with sodium hydroxide and aqueous ammonia; flame tests
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Writing ionic precipitation equations (IGCSE ch 4); Preparing an insoluble salt by precipitation

subtopics.name: Identifying anions: carbonate, chloride, bromide, iodide, nitrate, sulfate and sulfite
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Solubility rules for salts; precipitation reactions

subtopics.name: Identifying gases: ammonia, carbon dioxide, chlorine, hydrogen, oxygen and sulfur dioxide
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Reactions of acids and metals; litmus and limewater tests (Lower Secondary science)

subtopics.name: Acid–base titration technique and choosing suitable indicators
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Titration calculations (IGCSE ch 5); indicators and the pH scale (IGCSE ch 11)
